subject.title: Feature: fire session-memory hook on session reset/prune, not just compaction

question: Should OpenClaw standardize an awaitable pre-finalization lifecycle contract for automatic reset and maintenance prune, or limit the bundled session-memory behavior to reset-only capture first?
rationale: The choice determines plugin-visible hook semantics, whether destructive prune may wait for external/file writes, and whether the existing command-oriented hook remains the long-term abstraction.

options.title: Adopt a unified finalization contract
options.body: Specify reset and pre-prune reasons, bounded completion semantics, and duplicate-suppression rules before implementing both lifecycle paths.

options.title: Land reset-only capture first
options.body: Constrain the current work to daily/idle rollover and track pre-prune finalization as a separate contract proposal.

options.title: Keep capture command-driven
options.body: Retain the existing behavior and document external scheduled reset as the supported workaround.

recommendation.title: Adopt a unified finalization contract
recommendation.body: Specify reset and pre-prune reasons, bounded completion semantics, and duplicate-suppression rules before implementing both lifecycle paths.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history and related PR context connect them most directly to the hooks/plugins lifecycle boundary.
